findings.frozenDecision: 比亚迪 High-priority company_engine_override selection over 长城汽车/上汽集团
findings.postOutcomeFundamentalDiagnosis: The operating engine did not fail. BYD Q3 2022 revenue rose 115.59% YoY, attributable profit rose 350.26% YoY, and YTD attributable profit rose 281.13%. The frozen thesis correctly identified extraordinary earnings conversion, but the stock still underperformed lower-expectation OEM controls over the pre-registered 60d horizon.
findings.rootCause: V1.1 interpreted a de-rated 20d/60d price state plus realized profit/CFO acceleration as sufficient expectation room. The frozen valuation still required roughly 98% forecast 2023 earnings growth and about 35x 2023E PE, so the market could continue compressing the duration/quality premium even as near-term earnings beat the operating thesis.
findings.generalLesson: De-rating is not the same as low expectations. For premium compounders, expectation burden must eventually test the duration and intensity of superior growth embedded in valuation, not only near-term earnings conversion and recent relative-price weakness.

findings.frozenDecision: High-priority physical power-scarcity hypothesis / No selection because the weather shock was short-lived, thermal economics were weak, and power equities had already rerated sharply.
findings.label: physical_shock_without_durable_earnings_bridge_blocked
findings.generalLesson: A real physical shortage is not automatically an equity opportunity when the event half-life is short, the fuel/tariff spread is unresolved, and prices have already moved strongly.

findings.frozenDecision: Research hypothesis / No selection because Q3 physical memory pricing was still worsening despite strong backward-looking H1 profits.
findings.label: stale_earnings_do_not_override_worsening_physical_cycle
findings.generalLesson: Backward-looking strong earnings should not be used to bottom-fish a cycle while forward physical price/inventory evidence continues to deteriorate.

repeatedSameCompanyCases.interpretation: Premium valuation already encoded long-duration superior growth.
Even a substantial de-rating did not guarantee low expectations because the premium still embedded near-doubling forward earnings.

crossWindowExpectationDurationCheck.interpretation: Expectation-duration/quality-premium misread now repeats across time but only in the same company. This raises priority for cross-company validation but is not sufficient to create V1.2.

decision.reason: The expectation-duration issue repeated in BYD across two periods, but same-company repetition is not sufficiently general to justify a new generic gate.
decision.nextAction: Continue unchanged V1.1 on another independent window and seek cross-company/cross-industry evidence before versioning any expectation-duration mechanism.

prohibitedUses: Do not alter V1.1 using this 2022Q3 outcome.
Do not learn fixed PE, PEG, growth, momentum or drawdown thresholds from BYD.
Do not infer that de-rated premium companies are universally bad buys.
Do not create V1.2 until the same failure class repeats in a different company/industry or is otherwise supported by an independent causal test.
